findings.problem: Step A of the wave pattern now spells out `--task-text "<task title and description>"`, but Step B (implement) is written with an ellipsis (`--for implement ... --out`), which a literal reader takes as the flags of an older command. The same asymmetry is in orchestrator-prompt.md item 3 (`keryx skills resolve-context --for implement ... --out <...>/<task_id>.implement.resolved.json`). The implement dispatch is the one where a declared keyword matters most.
findings.impact: An orchestrator model that copies the implement line literally resolves without --task-text, so only glob conditions promote a reference; a document declared by keyword never becomes must_read for the implementer and no proof is required, with no warning (the resolver warns only on truncation).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the ellipsis in the implement lines of both files with the full flag list used in Step A (--files, --task-type, --task-text), or add one sentence saying the ellipsis stands for the same flags as Step A including --task-text.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk job-orchestrator/SKILL.md @@729,782: the -/+ pair adds --task-text to Step A only; the `--for implement ...` line is unchanged context. orchestrator-prompt.md @@112,160: item 1 gains --task-text, item 3 keeps `--for implement ... --out` and the added note describes the proof, not the flag.

findings.quote: const isPromoted = (entry: ContextEntry): boolean => entry.tier === "must_read" && entry.reason.startsWith("condition:");
findings.problem: The e2e test re-declares the predicate that decides which entries are 'promoted by a condition'. The production module already exports an identical `isPromoted` from src/gdskills/reference-proof.ts, and the same test file already imports `distinctWords` from that module. The definition of 'promoted' (tier plus the `condition:` reason prefix) is therefore stated in two places.
findings.impact: If the resolver's reason format or the promotion rule changes, the production predicate and this local copy can diverge. The e2e fixture builder (`buildResult`) would then cite proofs for a different set of entries than the validator obliges, and scenario failures would point at the fixture rather than at the changed rule. Only a maintenance cost today: the two definitions agree at this head.
findings.suggested_fix: Import `isPromoted` from "./reference-proof" next to `distinctWords`. If the intent is an independent oracle, keep the local copy but say so in a comment above it.
findings.evidence: reference-proof.ts at head: `export function isPromoted(entry: ContextEntry): boolean { return entry.tier === "must_read" && entry.reason.startsWith("condition:"); }`. The e2e test imports `import { distinctWords } from "./reference-proof";` and defines its own `isPromoted` at the harness section.

findings.problem: The ratio 20 (the anchored section must be under one twentieth of the document) is an unnamed literal repeated in three assertions (`styling.bytes / 20`, `Buffer.byteLength(text) / 20`, `theming.bytes / 20`), and the size tolerance `+ 2_000` is repeated four times in the fixture test. The file names its other sizes (STYLING_TARGET_BYTES, THEMING_TARGET_BYTES) but not these two.
findings.impact: If the fixture is retuned (for example the anchored sections grow), four to seven literals must be found and changed together, and a reader cannot tell that the three `/ 20` checks assert one rule: the budget counts the section, not the file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `const MAX_SECTION_SHARE = 1 / 20;` and `const SIZE_TOLERANCE_BYTES = 2_000;` beside the other fixture constants and use them in all assertions.
findings.evidence: Diff of src/gdskills/conditional-reads.e2e.test.ts: `/ 20` appears in the fixture test, scenario 1 and scenario 2; `+ 2_000` appears in the four upper-bound expectations of the fixture test.

findings.quote: expect(lines).toContain(`- ${THEMING_PATH} — project contract, declared, ${theming.bytes} bytes, sha256 ${theming.sha256.slice(0, 12)} (anchor "${THEMING_ANCHOR}", section ${theming.section_bytes} bytes)`);
findings.problem: The printed report an on_demand declared reference gets carries path, reason, bytes, sha and anchor, but not the declaration's description or condition, and the report has no undeclared list. renderResolutionMarkdown (unchanged apart from the anchor flag) is also what formatSkillsResolveContext returns to the interactive agent and what the CLI prints without --json. The description is the only text that tells a worker when to open an on_demand document (task-implementer SKILL.md: 'read on_demand ones only when the work touches them'), and the e2e test pins the line without it.
findings.impact: A worker that reads the Markdown form (the agent tool, or the CLI default) sees 'THEMING.md ... declared ... anchor "Theme tokens"' with nothing on what the document governs or when it applies, so the on-demand half of the feature (AC5: a task matching neither keeps description, anchor and condition) is only usable from the JSON form. AC5 itself is met in the entry record.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the description (and the condition, compactly) to the entry line for declared entries in renderResolutionMarkdown, add an 'undeclared' line when the list is non-empty, and update the e2e expectation; or state in the worker instructions that the JSON (--out) form is the one to read.
findings.evidence: e2e test at 'the printed report lists the promoted section and the on-demand document' asserts the exact line without description; resolve-context-command.ts renderResolutionMarkdown builds flags from index, linked, shadows, also_at and anchor only; formatSkillsResolveContext in metaproject-operations.ts returns renderResolutionMarkdown output plus warnings.

findings.quote: test("cap keeps promoted references: an over-cap promoted reference stays must_read and the warning gives the sizes, while rules keep flow 461 behaviour", async () => {
findings.problem: The test is the AC7 pin (promoted references are never demoted by the cap) but only one promoted reference competes with the cap. THEMING.md (size 6000) has the glob docs/** and the task files match src/**, so it is not promoted; it is on_demand because its condition does not match, not because the cap spared it. The assertion usedBytes: 12000 therefore mixes a 10000-byte promoted entry with a 2000-byte rule, and a mutant that demotes the second-largest promoted reference by the cap would not be caught.
findings.impact: AC7 says promoted references stay must_read under the cap. The test would still pass if the resolver demoted a second over-cap promoted reference, which is the case the criterion exists for.
findings.suggested_fix: Give THEMING.md the glob src/** so both STYLING.md and THEMING.md are promoted, then assert both stay must_read, the budget is exceeded, usedBytes equals the sum, and the warning names both sizes.
findings.evidence: Fixture in the slice lines 580-808: STYLING.md ruleText({ size: 10000 }) glob src/**; THEMING.md size 6000 glob docs/**; small.mdc 2000 bytes; maxBytes 4096; assertion expect(result.budget).toEqual({ limitBytes: 4096, usedBytes: 12000, exceeded: true, limitSource: "flag" }).

findings.quote: export async function resolveProjectContext(input: ResolveContextInput): Promise<ProjectContextResolution> {
findings.problem: Clean Code B1/B3. The function body is about 110 lines after this diff and mixes rule/skill selection, citation scanning, task-text truncation with its warning, reference resolution, budget arithmetic and result assembly. The diff added roughly 40 lines (task truncation warning, resolveReferences call, promoted-budget block). Inside it `declarations ?? []` is written three times (`(declarations ?? []).some(`, `declarations: declarations ?? [],`, `(declarations ?? []).map(`) next to a separate `declarations !== undefined` test for `undeclared`.
findings.impact: Each new feature layered on this function raises the cost of reading and testing it; the budget/promotion block cannot be unit-tested without a full resolve. Maintenance cost only.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind `const declared = declarations ?? [];` once. Extract the new blocks as small functions: `taskTextWarning(task, declared)` and `promotedBudgetWarning(references, used, cap)`. Pre-existing size is not charged to the diff; only the growth is.
findings.evidence: Diff slice-03, hunks '@@ 326,377 @@', '@@ 396,436 @@' and '@@ 438,552 @@' of src/gdskills/context-resolver.ts.

findings.problem: Clean Code B2. `collectContracts` now takes five positional parameters (projectRoot, cited, taken, declared, warnings), the diff adding the fifth; `readDeclaredFile(projectRoot, rootReal, rel, maxFileBytes)` and `undeclaredCitations(projectRoot, rootReal, cited, declared)` take four. Two sets of the same type (`taken`, `declared`) sit side by side, so a swapped call compiles. `projectRoot` and `rootReal` always travel together and rootReal is derived from projectRoot. `warnings: string[]` is an output argument.
findings.impact: A transposed `taken`/`declared` argument type-checks and silently changes which citations are listed. Maintenance cost.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass one options object (`{ projectRoot, cited, taken, declared }`) and return warnings alongside entries, as `resolveReferences` already does with `ResolvedReferences`.
findings.evidence: collectContracts signature in the diff; readDeclaredFile in reference-entries.ts; undeclaredCitations in references-check.ts. The caller passes `new Set([...taken, ...declaredPaths])` and `new Set((declarations ?? []).map(...))` in the same two positions.

findings.quote: const contracts = await collectContracts(projectRoot, cited, new Set([...taken, ...declaredPaths]), new Set((declarations ?? []).map((declaration) => declaration.path)), warnings);
findings.problem: resolveProjectContext gains task truncation, reference resolution, a promoted-bytes budget check and the `undeclared` output on top of rule, skill, bundled and contract collection; it is now roughly 110 lines with well over ten decision points. `declarations ?? []` is repeated three times, and the 'undefined means no file' versus '[]' distinction is carried by a nullable value.
findings.impact: The function is the place every future context feature lands; its length and the repeated null-coalescing make the budget arithmetic (used, promotedBytes, total, overCap) hard to follow and easy to misread.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind `const declared = declarations ?? [];` once, and move the reference part (truncation warning, resolveReferences, promoted-bytes cap warning) into a helper that returns {entries, total, warnings}.
findings.evidence: Diff hunks 'context-resolver.ts @@ 438,552' show the three `declarations ?? []` uses and the new tail of the function.

findings.problem: The hint is computed after importProjectRules for every text-mode run, including --dry-run (and a run where rules were refused). A dry run copies nothing, so the count describes the rules already installed, not the rules the command would import, under the comment 'Documents the imported rules cite but nothing declares'.
findings.impact: Trigger: `keryx skills import --rules <dir> --dry-run`. Outcome: the closing lines either say nothing about the rules about to be imported or report documents cited by unrelated, already-installed rules, so the operator reads a count that is not about the preview.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip the hint when args.includes("--dry-run"), or when result.rules holds no row with status imported or overwritten.
findings.evidence: Diff, runSkillsImportRulesCommand: `const json = args.includes("--json");` ... `if (!json) { const hint = await undeclaredCitationHint(process.cwd()); ... }`; no check of dryRun or of the result rows before it. undeclaredCitationHint reads only files on disk via scanCitations.

findings.quote: test("the synced copies carry the same schema as the bundled source", () => {
findings.problem: Two new test files assert the same invariant, 'the managed copies of the two output-contract schemas are byte-identical to the bundled source', each from its own hand-written path table. output-schema.test.ts keeps `SCHEMA_SOURCES` (source plus two copies per producer). skill-sync.test.ts keeps `schemaFiles` and `contractCopies`, which name the same four paths for the task-implementer and tests-creator output schemas.
findings.impact: Adding a third producer, or moving a contract copy, needs edits in both tables. A table that is missed still passes while the other one covers the file, so the drift is silent. The sync rule for these schemas has no single owner.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the byte-identity assertions in one file (skill-sync.test.ts already owns the bundled-to-managed mapping for instructions and schemas) and keep output-schema.test.ts to the schema-content checks. Alternatively export the path table from one file and import it in the other.
findings.evidence: output-schema.test.ts: `copies: [".metaproject/skills/gdskills/orchestration/task-implementer/output-contract.schema.json", ".metaproject/core/gdskills/contracts/task-implementer-output-contract.schema.json"]`. skill-sync.test.ts: `"orchestration/task-implementer/output-contract.schema.json"` in `schemaFiles`, and `["orchestration/task-implementer/output-contract.schema.json", "task-implementer-output-contract.schema.json"]` in `contractCopies`. Both resolve to the same managed files and assert `toBe(read(source))`.

findings.problem: readReferences calls loadReferences, and then checkReferences, which loads the same file again, scans every copied rule, and reads every declared document. The status loader, documented as a 'read-only snapshot' for the TUI sidebar and modal, now runs the full authoring checker on every load, and the declarations it returns and the findings it returns come from two separate reads.
findings.impact: Every refresh of the ProjectCtx status performs a second parse of references.json plus a read of all rule files and all declared documents (each up to the 262144-byte cap). The two reads can disagree if the file changes between them (declarations from one version, findings from another).
findings.suggested_fix: Let checkReferences accept the already loaded declarations (checkLoadedReferences(projectRoot, loaded)) and call it from readReferences, keeping checkReferences(projectRoot) as the thin wrapper that loads first.
findings.evidence: Diff, project-context-status.ts: `const loaded = await loadReferences(projectRoot); ... const report = await checkReferences(projectRoot);`; references-check.ts checkReferences begins with `const loaded = await loadReferences(projectRoot);`.

findings.problem: `loadProjectContextStatus` now runs the full `checkReferences` analysis whenever a `references.json` exists. That analysis reads every project rule (`scanCitations` over `listRuleRefs`, one `readFile` each), then inspects every declared document and every undeclared cited document (up to 262144 bytes each, read whole), then runs `extractSection` on each anchored one. `readReferences` calls `loadReferences`, and `checkReferences` calls it again. `listRuleRefs` also runs a second time next to the one already in the `Promise.all`. The TUI calls this function from `createProjectContextFeed`, whose default interval fires `poll` every 5000 ms with `setInterval`. The tick has no in-flight guard.
findings.impact: Trigger: a project that declares references, with the TUI open. It repeats N rule reads plus M document reads, M documents of up to 256 KB each, every 5 s for as long as the TUI lives, although the answer only changes when a file changes. If a poll takes longer than 5 s, for example on a slow or network disk, ticks overlap and reads pile up. The cost is small for typical projects. Projects without `references.json` pay only one ENOENT read.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the cheap parts in the poll (declarations and counts). Run the full `checkReferences` only when the modal's references tab is open or after an explicit reload, or cache the report keyed on the mtimes of `references.json`, the rules folder and the declared files. Also add a `polling` boolean to `poll` so a slow tick skips the next one.
findings.evidence: project-context-status.ts `readReferences` calls `loadReferences` then `checkReferences`; references-check.ts `checkReferences` calls `loadReferences`, `scanCitations` and `inspectDocument` again. src/tui/project-context-inspector.ts: `PROJECT_CONTEXT_POLL_MS = 5000` and `setInterval(() => { void tick(); }, ms)`.

findings.quote: async function readDeclaredFile(projectRoot: string, rootReal: string, rel: string, maxFileBytes: number): Promise<ReadOutcome> {
findings.problem: The sequence lstat, realpath, containment check, regular-file check, size cap, read is written three times in this slice with small differences: readDeclaredFile here (re-lstats the real path), inspectDocument in references-check.ts (stats the real path, different status vocabulary), and the inline loop in collectContracts. Each caller owns a different result vocabulary, and the same declared document is judged by both readDeclaredFile at resolve time and inspectDocument at check time.
findings.impact: A change to what counts as a readable document (for example a symlink or size rule) must be made in several places, and `references check` can accept a document that the resolver then rejects or the reverse, which makes the authoring tool an unreliable predictor of resolve behaviour. This is a maintenance cost; no divergence was demonstrated in the current code.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract one `inspectProjectDocument(projectRoot, rootReal, rel, maxBytes)` returning a tagged status plus text (the shape of Inspection in references-check.ts), place it next to the other filesystem helpers, and have reference-entries.ts map the status to a reject reason and references-check.ts map it to a finding.
findings.evidence: Diff: readDeclaredFile (reference-entries.ts) and inspectDocument (references-check.ts) both call lstat and realpath, test isPathInside(rootReal, real), check isFile and a byte cap from CONTRACT_MAX_BYTES, then readFile; collectContracts repeats the realpath and containment steps.

findings.quote: export async function resolveReferences(input: ResolveReferencesInput): Promise<ResolvedReferences> {
findings.problem: Clean Code B1. The function is about 46 lines (exceeds the 40-line guide) and mixes levels: duplicate-listing guard, file read, anchor-to-section byte accounting with its dead-anchor fallback and warning text, promotion decision, and entry construction in one loop body.
findings.impact: The dead-anchor fallback (whole file becomes the obligation) is a policy decision buried in a loop; changing it means editing the loop that also builds entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `obligationBytes(declaration, text, warnings): number` for the anchor block and `toEntry(declaration, read, reason, sectionBytes)` for the entry literal; keep the loop as guard, read, measure, promote, push.
findings.evidence: Diff slice-03, new file src/gdskills/reference-entries.ts, resolveReferences body.

findings.quote: const headings = section.available.length > 0 ? ` Headings in the file: ${section.available.join("; ")}.` : "";
findings.problem: When an anchor is not found, the warning lists every heading of the file with no cap. `references-check.ts` caps the same list at 12 (`headings.slice(0, 12)` and `", ..."`), so the two paths disagree. The warning is pushed into `ProjectContextResolution.warnings`, which is written to the JSON result, to `last.json`, and to stderr on every resolve.
findings.impact: Trigger: a declared anchor that does not match a heading in a large document, up to 262144 bytes with thousands of headings. Every resolve then emits a warning of tens to hundreds of kilobytes. The result is handed to workers as context, so one dead anchor repeats that text in each dispatch's prompt and in the recorded last-resolve file.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap the list the same way as references-check.ts, with the first 12 headings and a trailing "...". Share one helper for the truncated heading list.
findings.evidence: reference-entries.ts builds the string from the whole `section.available` array. references-check.ts uses `headings.slice(0, 12).join(", ")` and appends `", ..."` when there are more.

findings.problem: keywordOccurs builds a Unicode-aware whole-word regex with lookarounds over letters, digits and underscore, and escapes the keyword. The tests only use 'tailwinds are mentioned' and 'the pretailwind thing'. Digit adjacency (tailwind2), underscore adjacency (_tailwind), a non-ASCII neighbour letter, and a keyword with regex metacharacters (a.b versus axb, c++) are not pinned.
findings.impact: Dropping \p{N} or _ from the lookarounds, or the escape, keeps the suite green. A keyword such as c++ would then throw or match wrongly, and identifiers like tailwind2 would wrongly promote a document.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cases: keyword tailwind not matching in tailwind2, _tailwind and the Cyrillic-adjacent text; keyword a.b matching 'a.b' but not 'axb'; keyword c++ matching 'use c++ here' without throwing.
findings.evidence: Resolver tests in the slice (lines 580-808) use only the two ASCII phrases above. Production confirms escapeRegExp exists, so c++ does not crash, but nothing asserts it.

findings.problem: Several resolveReferences branches have no assertion in the diff: the taken collision (a declared path already listed as a rule or skill is skipped with a warning), the maxFileBytes limit (info.size > maxFileBytes), glob-before-keyword precedence in the reason, and the 'Headings in the file' text for a missing anchor. Coverage elsewhere in the repository was not searched, so this is limited to the slice.
findings.impact: Removing the taken check would list one file twice (as a rule and as a reference) and double its bytes in the budget. Changing > to >= or swapping glob and keyword order would change reasons the validator and the TUI print.
findings.suggested_fix: Add resolver cases: a declaration whose path is already a listed rule (expect one entry and a warning); a file of exactly maxFileBytes (accepted) and maxFileBytes+1 (skipped with warning); a declaration matching by both glob and keyword (expect condition:glob:<g>); a missing anchor warning that lists the headings.
findings.evidence: Read the resolver tests added in the slice and context-resolver.test.ts additions; none exercises these branches. Production branches read in reference-entries.ts.

findings.problem: The proof thresholds (40 characters, 3 shared words, 5 letters) have one source in code, but slice-01 restates them by hand in prose in the flow-orchestrator, job-orchestrator, task-implementer and tests-creator SKILL.md files, orchestrator-prompt.md, cli-reference.md, the apply-project-rules guide, the PRD, the AC file, live-run.md and the schema descriptions. skill-sync.test.ts guards the keywords (--task-text, the paragraph naming condition:, path, sha256, anchor, summary) and the byte equality of the bundled / managed / contract copies, but not the numbers.
findings.impact: Changing a threshold (the PRD itself expects tuning after the live run) needs a ten-file hand edit with nothing that fails when one is missed. F-001 is the first case of exactly this: the runbook already says two where the code says three, and every test is green.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the numbers in the instruction text, since a worker reads them there, but add a test next to skill-sync.test.ts that imports SUMMARY_MIN_CHARS, SUMMARY_MIN_SHARED_WORDS and WORD_MIN_LETTERS from reference-proof.ts and asserts that each instruction file, cli-reference.md and the guide contain the current values (and no other number in the sentence that carries them). Failing that, have the prose point at the CLI output for the threshold.
findings.evidence: src/gdskills/skill-sync.test.ts at head checks regexes for '--task-text' and the 'condition:' paragraph and the copy equality, and no numeric threshold. reference-proof.ts exports the three constants; live-run.md already disagrees with them (F-001).

findings.problem: Whether an entry is a promoted reference is decided by a string prefix of the free-text reason field. The producer is reference-entries.ts (`condition:glob:${glob}`, `condition:keyword:${keyword}`) in another module, with no shared constant or type; the entry already carries the structured field that says it is a declared reference (`condition`).
findings.impact: A change to the reason wording in reference-entries.ts, or another entry kind whose reason starts with 'condition:', silently turns the proof obligation off or on in the validator, which reads a --resolved file produced by a different command run.
findings.suggested_fix: Export the reason prefix from reference-entries.ts and build and test it there, or discriminate on `entry.condition !== undefined && entry.reason !== "declared"`; better, add a typed `promoted: true` field to ContextEntry for declared entries.
findings.evidence: Diff, reference-entries.ts: `reason: reason ?? "declared"` with promotionReason returning `condition:glob:${glob}` / `condition:keyword:${keyword}`; reference-proof.ts isPromoted matches on `entry.reason.startsWith("condition:")`. The two files share no constant.

findings.problem: WORD_MIN_LETTERS is exported and used in the failure message ('words of ${WORD_MIN_LETTERS} or more letters'), but distinctWords hard-codes `{5,}` in its regular expression. The threshold exists in two places and only one of them is enforced.
findings.impact: Changing WORD_MIN_LETTERS (it is exported, so a test or another module may change expectations around it) changes the message but not the rule, so the validator reports a threshold it does not apply.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the pattern from the constant: new RegExp(`\\p{L}{${WORD_MIN_LETTERS},}`, "gu"), constructed once at module level.
findings.evidence: Diff: `export const WORD_MIN_LETTERS = 5;` and the literal `/\p{L}{5,}/gu` in distinctWords; WORD_MIN_LETTERS is read only in wordsFailure's message.

findings.problem: The summary proof is well covered for length 28 versus 40, the 2/3 shared words boundary, case, and Cyrillic. Not pinned: code-point counting (an astral character counts as one, not two), NFC normalisation in distinctWords, the three-tier fallback of pickProofItem beyond the n/a-plus-followed pair, the Math.min clamp is pinned only for 1 and 0 section words, and the letter threshold {5,} (a four-letter and a five-letter word on the boundary).
findings.impact: Replacing Array.from with .length, dropping .normalize('NFC'), or changing {5,} to {4,} would pass the suite. A decomposed accent in a Russian or French summary would then fail to match the composed section word.
findings.suggested_fix: Add: a 39-code-point summary containing an emoji (rejected by length) and a 40-code-point one (accepted); a decomposed (NFD) summary word matching a composed section word; a section whose only shared word has exactly four letters (must not count).
findings.evidence: Read resolved-context-check.test.ts additions in the slice (lines 1522-1830) against reference-proof.ts at head.

findings.problem: Clean Code E2. The cap of 12 listed headings appears twice in one expression (`slice(0, 12)` and `headings.length > 12 ? ", ..."`) with no name.
findings.impact: Changing one literal without the other drops or adds the trailing ellipsis incorrectly.
findings.suggested_fix: `const MAX_LISTED_HEADINGS = 12;` and use it in both places.
findings.evidence: declarationFindings, anchor-not-found message: `${headings.length > 12 ? ", ..." : ""}`.
